record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: For the family M_m of planar polynomial differential systems with exactly m monomial vector-field terms, find upper and lower bounds for H_M[m], the maximum possible number of limit cycles among systems in M_m.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. (i) Find upper and lower bounds for HM[m].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer m ≥ 1, let M_m denote the family of planar polynomial differential systems
    dx/dt = P(x,y),    dy/dt = Q(x,y),
where P and Q are real polynomials in x and y, and where the total number of monomials appearing in (P,Q) (counted across both components together, with each nonzero term contributing one monomial) is exactly m. A limit cycle of such a system is an isolated periodic orbit in the phase plane.

Define
    H_M[m] = sup{ number of limit cycles of the system X : X ∈ M_m },
where the supremum is taken over all systems in M_m (and is allowed to be +∞).

Problem. Determine nontrivial upper and lower bounds for H_M[m] as a function of m. In particular, give explicit functions f(m) and g(m) such that
    f(m) ≤ H_M[m] ≤ g(m)
for all sufficiently large m, and clarify whether H_M[m] is finite for every m.
artifact.status_search_result: The monomial-count variant of Hilbert's 16th problem is an active research direction. Recent work establishes lower bounds (at least quadratic in m, with explicit values for small m ≤ 10), but no matching upper bounds are known and even the finiteness of H_M[m] for all m is not established. The problem is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: On a variant of Hilbert's 16th problem
status_evidence.snippet: The number of limit cycles increases at least quadratically with m and good lower bounds are obtained for m ≤ 10.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides lower bounds on H_M[m], showing growth at least quadratic in m, but matching upper bounds remain unknown.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Hilbert's 16th problem on the number of limit cycles of planar polynomial systems remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Even the classical Hilbert number H(n) (by degree) is not known to be finite, so the monomial variant H_M[m] remains open.
